$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only one that can tell a scorer which keeps definite false
positives apart from unattributed findings from one that folds them together. It reports two findings
that match no plant, one against the clean control and one against a seeded file, and only the first
derivation: The verdict carries eleven findings: the nine planted rows at their firing lines, an M3 against
seeded/orders.service.spec.ts:36, and a second H10 against clean/profile.spec.ts:26. All eleven name a
file, so unlocated is 0, reported is 11 and hits is 9, with criticalHits 4 of 4 and misses empty.
M3 matches no plant, because ground truth plants no M3 anywhere. Its file is a seeded fixture, whose
planted array is non-empty, so it is not a clean path and it lands in unattributed: 1. That is the
case ground-truth.json's own history describes, where this plant was recorded as M3 until the H10 row
The second H10 cannot match the planted H10, because matching requires the reported file to end with
the planted file's basename and clean/profile.spec.ts does not end with orders.service.spec.ts. Its
file IS the clean control, whose planted array is empty, so it lands in falsePositives: 1. Ground
truth lists exactly this shape under commonFalsePositives for the clean fixture.
The counts the harness derives from these: recall 9/9 = 1.00, CRITICAL recall 4/4 = 1.00,
nonFalsePositiveRate (11 - 1)/11 = 0.9091 against a 0.80 floor. Folding the unattributed M3 into the
numerator would give (11 - 2)/11 = 0.8182 instead, which is the difference this case exists to pin.
score and recommendation come from the verdict: 100 - 4x10 - 5x5 - 1x2 - 1x1 = 32, Block on Criticals.
No finding names a file outside the review set, so outOfScope is 0 and falsePositives is unchanged by it.
